t.2.6.1: When the family priest had gone, Rāma, having bathed and with his mind restrained, approached Nārāyaṇa together with his wide-eyed wife.
t.2.6.2: Then, raising the vessel of oblation reverently to his head, he duly poured the clarified butter into the blazing fire as an offering to the great deity.
t.2.6.3: Having eaten the remainder of that oblation and prayed for what was dear to himself, meditating on the god Nārāyaṇa, he lay upon a well-spread bed of kuśa grass.
t.2.6.5: When only one watch of the night remained, he awoke and had the entire adornment of his dwelling carried out.
t.2.6.4: Having become restrained in speech, with his mind held in check, the son of the best of men lay down together with Vaidehī in the splendid sanctuary of Viṣṇu.
t.2.6.6: There, hearing the pleasing words of the sūtas, māgadhas and bards, he performed the morning twilight worship and, with his mind restrained, recited his prayers in a low voice.
t.2.6.7: Bowing low with his head, he praised Madhusūdana, and, clad in spotless linen, he had the twice-born recite their blessings.
t.2.6.8: Then their proclamation of the auspicious day, deep and sweet, echoed by the sound of musical instruments, filled Ayodhyā.
t.2.6.9: Then, hearing that Rāghava had undertaken the fast together with Vaidehī, all the people dwelling in Ayodhyā rejoiced.
t.2.6.10: Then all the townsfolk, having heard of Rāma's consecration and seeing that the night had given way to dawn, once more set about adorning the city with surpassing splendour.
t.2.6.12: In the shops of the merchants, rich with wares of many kinds, and in the prosperous and splendid houses of the householders,
t.2.6.11: On the temples of the gods, which shone like the peaks of white clouds, at the crossroads and along the streets, on the sacred shrines and on the watchtowers,
t.2.6.13: Then in all the assembly halls, and on the conspicuous trees as well, colorful flags and banners were raised high.
t.2.6.15: As Rāma's consecration drew near, the people talked with one another about Rāma's consecration at the crossroads and in their homes.
t.2.6.14: And here and there they heard the voices of troupes of actors and dancers, and of singers singing, delightful to the mind and to the ear.
t.2.6.16: Even the children, playing in groups at the doors of the houses, talked among themselves about nothing but Rāma's consecration.
t.2.6.17: For Rāma's consecration, the citizens made the royal highway splendid, strewn with offerings of flowers and perfumed with the fragrance of incense.
t.2.6.18: And, anxious lest night should fall, they likewise set up tree-shaped lamps all along the streets everywhere, so as to make them bright.
t.2.6.19: Having thus adorned the city, the inhabitants of that city waited eagerly for Rāma's consecration as heir apparent.
t.2.6.20: Gathering together in groups at the crossroads and in the assembly halls, all of them, conversing with one another there, praised the lord of the people.
t.2.6.21: Ah, how great-souled is this king, the delight of the Ikṣvāku race, who, knowing himself to be old, will consecrate Rāma in the kingship!
t.2.6.22: We are all truly blessed, for Rāma, who has seen the high and the low of the world, will be our king and protector for a long time.
t.2.6.24: Long may he live, the righteous-souled and sinless King Daśaratha, by whose grace we shall behold Rāma consecrated!
t.2.6.23: Rāghava is free of arrogance in mind, learned, righteous in spirit and devoted to his brothers; and just as he is affectionate toward his brothers, so too is he toward us.
t.2.6.25: Then the country folk, who had heard the news and had come even from all directions, heard the townspeople speaking in this manner.
t.2.6.26: The people of the countryside, having come to the city from all directions to witness Rāma's consecration, filled Rāma's city.
t.2.6.27: From those multitudes of people streaming about, a roar was heard there, like the roar of the ocean whose force swells high on the days of the moon's change.
t.2.6.28: Then that city, resembling the abode of Indra, thronged on every side by country folk who had come eager to see, shone filled with clamor, like the waters of the ocean teeming with sea creatures.
